elements.element: Customer is subject to no exclusivity obligation in favor of Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly states that Vendor is non-exclusive and that Customer has no exclusivity obligation. Section 12.3 independently confirms that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment.

elements.element: Customer is not required to use Vendor as its sole supplier.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly states that Customer has no sole-supplier obligation, and Section 12.3 preserves Customer's freedom to engage any supplier.

elements.element: If Customer is bound by exclusivity, its scope is limited to an expressly defined product category.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the operative language imposes no exclusivity at all, so there is no exclusivity requiring a product-category limitation.

elements.element: If Customer is bound by exclusivity, its duration is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Sections 2.2 and 12.3 establish that Customer has no exclusivity commitment, so no exclusivity period exists that could exceed 12 months.

elements.element: If Customer is bound by exclusivity, it terminates automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet an applicable service level.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Customer is not bound by exclusivity. Accordingly, no service-level termination mechanism is required to release Customer from exclusivity.

elements.element: If Customer is bound by exclusivity, it terminates automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet an applicable delivery date.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Customer is not bound by exclusivity. Accordingly, no delivery-date termination mechanism is required to release Customer from exclusivity.

result.reason: The operative language clearly achieves the preferred no-exclusivity position; the fallback limitations are also satisfied conditionally because no exclusivity exists. However, the redline unnecessarily deletes the original statement that Vendor's provider appointment lasts “throughout the term,” altering an appointment-duration term unrelated to exclusivity. The express no-exclusivity sentence in Section 2.2 is also somewhat duplicative of the non-exclusive appointment and Section 12.3.
